source.title: Regularizing Deep Neural Networks with Stochastic Estimators of Hessian Trace
source.authors: Yucong Liu; Shi-Xing Yu; Tong Lin

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including experiments and conclusion.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests an added Hessian-trace regularizer and reports test performance, but its results do not test the claim versions: it does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, architecture comparisons, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout effects, magnitude-aware sharpness against generalization gaps, or removal of memorized examples. The reported regularizer results are outside the mapped versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports experiments adding SEHT Hessian-trace regularization and test accuracy/perplexity outcomes. These do not bear on a listed version; comparisons to other regularizers are not evidence about the listed interventions.
record.test_reason: The main Hessian-trace regularization experiments fall outside the versions, but Section 5.1.2 reports that combining SEHT-D with dropout lowers CIFAR-100 accuracy. This qualitative classifier result bears on V6 in a new regularization setting.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that SEHT-H and SEHT-D yield promising held-out performance and outperform several tested alternatives. They also report that SEHT-D combines poorly with dropout on CIFAR-100.
record.recipe_differences: Adds a stochastic Hessian-trace penalty; does not implement the mapped claim interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported SEHT outcomes vary with estimator, probability and iteration settings; the paper notes increased maxIter and probability can improve test accuracy at greater time cost.

fits_no_version.finding: SEHT improves reported test accuracy or perplexity over baseline on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and WikiText-2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Penalizing stochastic estimates of Hessian trace can improve held-out performance in these tested models and training recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: DropBlock yields 89.23% CIFAR-10 accuracy versus 94.00% for the weight-decay baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Structured feature-map masking can hurt ResNet-18 accuracy under this recipe; this does not directly establish the effect of ordinary dropout named in V6.

record.problems: The paper motivates the method partly with a generalization bound stated for linear models and extends that motivation to deep networks; it says future work could provide a multi-layer generalization bound. Reported experiments compare test metrics, not training-test gaps.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: the reported SEHT and comparator results do not measure any listed claim version, so they are not extracted as version rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout benefits without SEHT, very small training sets, underfitting from excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its association with training-test gaps, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

missing.what: The qualitative result that combining SEHT-D with dropout lowers CIFAR-100 accuracy. Extract the stated direction while marking the numerical values and exact baseline/configuration as unspecified. The record incorrectly dismisses all results as unrelated to the versions.

record.verdict_notes: Hessian-trace penalization does not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness correlation. Dropout used to subsample the Hessian estimator is distinct from classifier dropout. The CIFAR-100 dropout comparison is qualitative and incompletely specified, so it supports only a narrow scope qualification.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image models and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the stated tuning conditions.
Large versus small batch performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects in the stated classifier regimes and its removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness tracking the training-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.

relationships.condition: WRN-28-10 on CIFAR-100 with SEHT-D and dropout.
relationships.reason: Section 5.1.2 explicitly reports lower accuracy when SEHT-D is combined with dropout, indicating an unfavorable interaction in this regime. This verdict rests on text; no row records the comparison, and numerical results and the precise comparison configuration are unspecified.
relationships.display_finding: The authors reported lower accuracy from the combination without numerical results or a precise description of the comparison settings. This result has not been independently checked.
